home.title: Charting the schizophrenic brain with multimodal neuroimaging and machine intelligence
home.lead: The MSB group, led by Dr. Yunshuang Fan at the School of Life Science and Technology, UESTC, investigates the neural mechanisms of schizophrenia using multimodal MRI, connectomics and artificial intelligence — towards individualized diagnosis and treatment.
home.hl.title: Research Highlights
home.hl.1.p: Integrating structural, functional and diffusion MRI to map gray-matter alterations and dysconnectivity across the course of schizophrenia.
home.hl.2.p: Characterizing aberrant brain network organization — gradients, effective connectivity and temporal dynamics — from childhood-onset to chronic stages.
home.hl.3.p: Machine-learning on individual-level connectomes to predict symptoms, treatment response and illness trajectories.

research.title: Research
research.lead: We combine advanced magnetic resonance imaging and artificial intelligence to understand the brain mechanisms of schizophrenia and to develop precision diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
research.d1.p: Using multimodal MRI (sMRI, fMRI, dMRI) we systematically map gray-matter abnormalities and structural-functional dysconnectivity in drug-naïve first-episode and early-onset schizophrenia, revealing disease-specific cortical thickness and connectivity signatures.
research.d2.p: We study the brain as a dynamic networked system: macroscale functional gradients of the thalamus and cortex, effective connectivity across anti-correlated networks, and temporal dynamics of intrinsic activity — and how they break down in psychosis.
research.d3.p: We build individual-specific functional connectome biomarkers and connectome-based brain-age models to predict positive/negative symptom trajectories and treatment response (e.g., to risperidone) in first-episode schizophrenia.
research.d4.p: Extending beyond the cortex, we investigate gray-matter and connectivity alterations within cerebellum–neostriatum–cortical networks and their role in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia and related movement disorders.
research.collab: We collaborate closely with Prof. Huafu Chen's brain imaging team at the Key Laboratory for NeuroInformation of the Ministry of Education.
